frameworkName: NIST SP 800-161r1 (Cyber Supply Chain Risk Management)
licenseNote: Public domain (U.S. Government publication). Summaries below are original, written for this application - they are not reproductions of NIST publication text.
demonstrationSubsetDisclaimer: This is an illustrative subset for portfolio demonstration purposes, not full framework coverage.

controls.title: Supply chain risk management strategy
controls.summary: The organization maintains a documented strategy for identifying and managing risk introduced by suppliers, including this vendor's tier in the supply chain.
controls.validationGuidance: Look for a named owner, review cadence, and explicit criteria for classifying supplier criticality.

controls.title: Supplier due diligence prior to engagement
controls.summary: Vendors perform documented security and risk due diligence on their own critical suppliers before engaging them.
controls.validationGuidance: Evidence should show a repeatable pre-engagement review process, not a one-time or informal check.

controls.title: Contractual flow-down of security requirements
controls.summary: Security and privacy requirements are contractually flowed down to the vendor's own subprocessors and subcontractors.
controls.validationGuidance: Check that the DPA or MSA explicitly requires downstream parties to meet equivalent security obligations.

controls.title: Fourth-party (subprocessor) visibility
controls.summary: The vendor maintains and discloses a current list of subprocessors that can access customer data or systems.
controls.validationGuidance: Confirm the list is dated, includes purpose and data access scope per subprocessor, and has a defined update/notification process.

controls.title: Component and dependency provenance
controls.summary: The vendor can identify the origin and integrity of critical software components (e.g. via SBOM) used in the delivered product.
controls.validationGuidance: Presence of an SBOM or equivalent dependency inventory is strong evidence; absence is a gap, not an automatic fail for lower-criticality vendors.

controls.title: Supply chain incident notification
controls.summary: The vendor commits, contractually or in policy, to timely notification of security incidents that could affect the customer through the supply chain.
controls.validationGuidance: Look for a specific notification timeframe (e.g. 72 hours) rather than vague 'reasonable time' language.

controls.title: Vendor personnel security for privileged access
controls.summary: Personnel with privileged access to customer systems or data undergo background screening and access review appropriate to their access level.
controls.validationGuidance: Evidence should distinguish general employee screening from screening specific to privileged-access roles.

controls.title: Counterfeit and integrity controls for hardware/firmware
controls.summary: Where the vendor supplies hardware or firmware, controls exist to verify authenticity and detect tampering before deployment.
controls.validationGuidance: Not applicable to pure SaaS vendors - mark NOT_APPLICABLE with justification rather than treating as a gap.

controls.title: Business continuity and resilience of the supply chain
controls.summary: The vendor has tested continuity plans that account for disruption to its own critical suppliers, not just its own infrastructure.
controls.validationGuidance: Look for evidence of an actual test or exercise, not only a written plan.

controls.title: Supply chain risk reassessment on material change
controls.summary: Supplier risk is reassessed when a material change occurs - ownership change, new subprocessor, geographic change - rather than only on a fixed annual cycle.
controls.validationGuidance: This is a common gap even in vendors with mature annual review programs; check specifically for an event-driven trigger, not just cadence.

controls.title: Right-to-audit or independent assurance
controls.summary: The contract grants a right to audit, or accepts independent third-party assurance (e.g. SOC 2 Type II) in lieu of direct audit rights.
controls.validationGuidance: A current, unqualified SOC 2 Type II opinion is generally sufficient in place of a direct audit right for most criticality tiers.

controls.title: Secure offboarding and data return/destruction
controls.summary: The vendor has a documented process for returning or destroying customer data at contract termination, with confirmation provided to the customer.
controls.validationGuidance: Look for a defined timeframe and a written confirmation/attestation step, not just a general destruction clause.
